changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail buyers, especially store operations and the COO: 'One system for the tills and the website.' One customer, one basket: an online order can be returned at the till, and the customer record and loyalty work in both channels. Back the line with a live demo of an online order being returned at a store till, step by step, instead of a platform diagram.
changes.why: The current M3 line met silence, the head of store operations called it 'that's a diagram.' and asked how a return works at the till, the customer kept saying 'One system for the tills and the website.', and we described the till return but never showed it.

changes.change: For retail COO and store-operations buyers, add a single-accountability line with a rollout proof point. Wording: 'One team accountable for your tills and your website, from install to go-live, with no two vendors pointing at each other.' Pair it with a standard store rollout plan that covers dates, who does the installs, and what happens to the old tills. Name the accountable party for installs explicitly, and do not answer 'a partner' without naming who owns the outcome.
changes.why: Angela said 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.', our install answer was that 'we'd bring in a partner' and nobody on our side had run a store rollout, the customer asked for a dated rollout plan, and Adyen pitched 'one platform for the tills and the website, on one contract' with people who'd done store rollouts.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail COOs: replace 'see our customer stories' with an offer to talk to a peer, for example 'Talk to a retailer who has rolled us out across their stores.' Keep named retail references ready to take a call on short notice.
changes.why: The COO asked 'can I talk to them?', 'we couldn't set up a call in time.', and the competitor named retailers Angela knew, so a customer-stories link was weaker proof than a callable peer.

changes.change: Retail opener for operations buyers: lead with the store-side pain rather than checkout conversion. Example: 'When a customer brings an online order back to the store, your staff should be able to refund it at the till, and your loyalty program should know it is the same customer.'
changes.why: The trigger was the store being unable to see the online order and a loyalty launch that failed because store and web were two customer records, and the evaluation moved from web to stores, while we were still pitching web checkout.
